tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (timeouts, latency, memory full, error replies) rather than implementation details, explicitly lists many trigger contexts including cases where the operator doesn't name the domain directly, clarifies scope exclusions (not for create/size/migrate), and remains a concise paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an operator is investigating a problem with an Amazon ElastiCache cache, or with any Valkey, Redis OSS or Memcached cache on AWS, even if they only describe the symptom. Triggers include application timeouts or latency talking to the cache, session or cache writes failing, high cache CPU or one hot shard, memory full, keys disappearing or a falling hit rate...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body jumps directly into domain-specific procedures (AWS CLI calls, specific metric names, PromQL delegation logic) without explaining general concepts like what ElastiCache or CloudWatch are. It assumes the agent knows AWS basics and focuses on non-obvious specifics.
tests.evidence: Group-level aggregates hide skew. Always break down by node or shard.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference material (metric thresholds, error tables, diagnosis rows, PromQL queries) is consistently offloaded to references/ files rather than embedded in the body, even within conditional branches like Step 1's deployment-type decision.
tests.evidence: Load [references/diagnosis-table.md](references/diagnosis-table.md) now; it is required for every investigation.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five reference files are linked with markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a specific condition for when to load it, such as cache type/engine or when an error reply is present.
tests.evidence: When the operator quotes an engine error reply, or the error metrics show one, load [references/error-strings.md](references/error-strings.md) to map it to its cause.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md without absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, destructive-risk operations (read-only rule, exact AWS CLI calls, exact Logs Insights query) are prescribed exactly, while flexible judgment areas (choosing which lookalike to rule out, how to phrase remediation) leave room for agent reasoning with rationale given (e.g., why read-only matters, why baseline windows matter).
tests.evidence: Read-only. Never run `modify-*`, `reboot-*`, `test-failover`... Present every change as a recommendation for the operator to run, with its impact.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Step 1 clearly designates a default metrics path per deployment type (OpenTelemetry for node-based Valkey vs classic metrics for serverless/Redis/Memcached) rather than listing all options as equal.
tests.evidence: Node-based Valkey: load [references/otel-promql.md]... Serverless (any engine), Redis OSS, Memcached, or gaps in the OpenTelemetry path: load [references/classic-metrics.md]

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable diagnostic procedure (identify deployment, check events, rule out lookalikes, check config, validate, report) applicable to any ElastiCache incident, not a one-off instance-specific task.
tests.evidence: Name the root cause of an ElastiCache incident from evidence, rule out the lookalike cause that produces the same symptom, and give the operator a fix.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a detailed Gotchas section with concrete, non-obvious environment-specific facts (CPU metric semantics, MOVED vs READONLY behavior, connection churn interpretation).
tests.evidence: A high rate of `HELLO`/`CLIENT SETINFO`/`AUTH`/`PING` with no data commands is what each *new* connection sends. Current connections stay flat because each connection lives only milliseconds.

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill provides an explicit five-part report structure for its structured output (root cause, evidence, ruled out, remediation, gaps), satisfying the need for a template.
tests.evidence: Always give all five parts, even when the cause looks obvious. 1. Root cause... 2. Evidence... 3. Ruled out... 4. Remediation... 5. Gaps

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The report template in Step 6 is short (5 bullet points, well under 20 lines) and stays inline in the body appropriately.
tests.evidence: 1. Root cause: one sentence naming the mechanism, not the symptom. 2. Evidence... 3. Ruled out... 4. Remediation... 5. Gaps

tests.reasoning: Step 5 explicitly instructs the agent to validate its own draft findings against checklist criteria before reporting, including checking that evidence is quoted not estimated and lookalikes are ruled out with evidence.
